text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Parliamentary Chairman Ivan Gasparovic has called an extraordinary session of parliament for Thursday. The only item on the agenda will be an opposition motion for the dismissal of Interior Minister Gustav Krajci.
- Only 4,809 privatisation bonds have been matched in anomymous trades since the beginning of the year, compared with 232,954 bonds sold in direct trades.

- The government is expected to discuss at its regular Tuesday session the possible impacts of some Czech import-related measures on Czech-Slovak trade with food and consumer goods. The preliminary agenda does not include any other major economic item.
- Local money market dealers do not expect a significant decrease in interbank rates in the near future due to a continued liquidity shortage on the market.

SME - Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar has officially invited opposition leaders for a round table discussion scheduled for Wednesday. All opposition parties except the Party of the Democratic left (SDL) said they would not hold any talks with Meciar unless he dismisses Interior Minister Gustav Krajci.

- Czech Minister of Trade and Industry Karel Kuhnl said Slovakia's introduction of quotas on Czech products, such as the recently adopted quotas on beer, could endanger the existence of the Czech-Slovak customs union and have a negative influence economies of both countries.

PRACA - The total cost of the failed referendums on NATO membership and presidential elections last month has yet to be calculated but are expected to be higher than the originally planned 147 million crowns.
- President Michal Kovac on Monday met with leaders of opposition parties to discuss the internal political situation after the two failed referendums.
- Premier Meciar has accused the Czech Republic of repeatedly breaking the customs union agreement by implementing unilateral protectionist measures aimed at improving its trade balance.
